edges.cite: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools (Aho et al.), sec. 1.2: the parser produces a syntax tree that the semantic-analysis and IR-generation phases consume
edges.note: The AST is the load-bearing intermediate representation handed between the pipeline's front-end phases.
The validate-input tactic (filtering + canonicalization) constrains escape handling: sequences must be decoded to canonical form exactly once before checks, or double-decoding bypasses validation.
SAX-style parsers announce parse events to registered handlers rather than being invoked procedurally - implicit invocation applied inside a parser.

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), sec. 1.2: lexical analysis is the first phase of the canonical compiler phase structure
edges.note: First stage of the reference pipeline; every later phase depends on its token stream.

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), ch. 4: LR parsing presented as the standard bottom-up method for the syntax-analysis phase
edges.note: Table-driven realization of the pipeline's parsing phase (yacc/bison lineage).

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), ch. 4 contrasts top-down (recursive-descent/LL) and bottom-up (LR) parsing as the two method families
edges.note: The canonical bottom-up counterpart of hand-written top-down parsing.
The longest-match rule is what makes the pipeline's lexical phase deterministic when token patterns overlap.
The standard token-selection rule applied inside a lexer's match loop.

edges.cite: Ford, 'Packrat Parsing: Simple, Powerful, Lazy, Linear Time' (ICFP 2002): recursive descent with memoization of intermediate parsing results
edges.note: Recursive descent over PEGs made linear-time via per-position memoization.
A linear-time realization of the pipeline's syntax-analysis phase for parsing expression grammars.
Parser-domain realization of the exception-handling availability tactic: detect the syntax error, resynchronize on a designated token, continue in a known state.

edges.cite: Hutton & Meijer, 'Monadic Parser Combinators': combinators compose recursive descent parsers as first-class functional values
edges.note: The functional idiom whose composed result is a recursive descent parser.
A functional-language realization of the pipeline's syntax-analysis phase (parsec lineage).

edges.cite: Nystrom, Crafting Interpreters, 'Compiling Expressions': Pratt parsing presented as the expression-parsing companion embedded in recursive descent
edges.note: Top-down operator-precedence parsing slotted into a recursive descent skeleton.
Both solve infix precedence: Pratt via binding powers and bounded recursion, shunting-yard via an explicit operator stack.
Expression-parsing technique used inside the pipeline's syntax-analysis phase.
The emit/unparse stage of compiler back ends, source formatters, and code generators - the inverse of the front-end phases, operating on the same AST.
The interactive driver over an interpretation engine plus persistent evaluation environment - the canonical front end of interpreter-organized systems (Lisp lineage).

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), ch. 4: recursive descent as a standard top-down method for the syntax-analysis phase
edges.note: The hand-written realization of the pipeline's parsing phase.

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), ch. 3: token classes are specified as regular expressions from which lexical analyzers are generated
edges.note: The specification notation the pipeline's lexical phase is built from.
Pattern matching is the workhorse implementation of the filtering/checking step of the validate-input security tactic.

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), ch. 3: lexers are specified by and generated from regular expressions (Lex)
edges.note: Regex defines the token patterns the lexer recognizes.
A variant front-end organization that collapses the pipeline's lexical and syntactic phases into one grammar.
Eliminates the separate tokenization component of the classic two-stage front end.

edges.cite: Fowler, Domain-Specific Languages, 'Semantic Model': the model a DSL parse populates is usually a Domain Model (PoEAA)
edges.note: The DSL's semantic model is an implementation-level instance of the Domain Model pattern.

edges.cite: Fowler, Domain-Specific Languages: explicitly distinguishes the parse-shaped syntax tree from the semantic model the parse populates
edges.note: Parse builds the AST; population translates it into the semantic model.
Dijkstra's stack-based expression-parsing technique used inside the syntax-analysis phase (ALGOL compiler heritage).

edges.cite: Compilers (Aho et al.), sec. 1.2: the symbol table is the shared structure read and written by all compiler phases
edges.note: The cross-phase shared state the reference pipeline depends on.

edges.cite: Fowler, PoEAA, Template View: the pattern is implemented by server pages / templating technology interpolating markers embedded in static markup
edges.note: The template engine is the mechanism-level realization of the Template View presentation pattern.

edges.cite: Nystrom, Crafting Interpreters, Part II ('A Tree-Walk Interpreter'): tree walking as the direct implementation of an interpretation engine executing the parsed program
edges.note: Implementation-level realization of the interpreter organization: engine + pseudo-program (AST) + execution state.
The pseudo-program the engine walks is the AST.
Text-only channels and payload formats (SMTP/MIME, JSON, XML) can carry binary message bodies only through Base64-style re-encoding.

edges.cite: Tanenbaum & Wetherall, Computer Networks, data link layer framing: bit stuffing (HDLC) named as a standard framing method
edges.note: Data-link-layer framing mechanism the layered protocol stack rests on.

edges.cite: Tanenbaum & Wetherall, Computer Networks: the framing section presents byte count, byte stuffing, and bit stuffing as alternative framing methods
edges.note: Bit-granular vs byte-granular delimiter transparency.

edges.cite: Tanenbaum & Wetherall, Computer Networks, framing: flag bytes with byte stuffing (PPP, SLIP) as a standard data link framing method
edges.note: Frame delimiting at the link layer of the stack.
The escape-marker mechanism applied at the frame/byte level: reserved delimiter plus escape byte instead of backslash notation.
Hashing/signing structured data is only sound when each abstract value has exactly one byte encoding; canonical forms (DER, JCS RFC 8785) exist for this tactic.
Digital signatures over structured messages presuppose a canonical encoding so any party can re-serialize and re-verify.
Lets an HTTP connection act as a stream connector for bodies of unknown total length (RFC 9112 transfer coding).
A stream of length-prefixed chunks with a zero-length terminating chunk.

edges.cite: Cheshire & Baker, 'Consistent Overhead Byte Stuffing' (SIGCOMM 1997): COBS presented as a byte stuffing algorithm with tightly bounded worst-case overhead
edges.note: Byte stuffing re-engineered for fixed worst-case expansion.
Data-link framing for serial and packet links where worst-case frame expansion must be bounded.
The client-prediction/server-snapshot loop (Quake model) depends on delta-compressed state snapshots against the last acknowledged baseline to fit bandwidth.
Transmits/stores differences instead of full values, cutting bandwidth and storage on hot paths.

edges.cite: Tanenbaum & Wetherall, Computer Networks: byte-count framing is one of the canonical data link framing methods
edges.note: Record delimitation mechanism for layered byte-stream protocols.

edges.cite: Tanenbaum & Wetherall, Computer Networks: framing section presents byte count and stuffing-based framing as alternatives
edges.note: Count-based vs delimiter-based message boundary recovery.
Checking a fixed signature at an interface is a minimal validity/reasonableness check on input format before further processing - the sanity-checking tactic at file granularity.
File-based integration relies on self-identifying formats so consumers can verify what kind of file they were handed independent of name/extension.
Fixing wire byte order (the big-endian network convention) with explicit host-to-wire conversion is the adhere-to-standards integrability tactic applied at the data-representation level.
REST's resource identification rides on RFC 3986 URIs, whose syntax reserves delimiter characters and delegates all other octets to percent-encoding.
An escape scheme with % as the marker and two hex digits as the code, per URI component.
The simplest hand-rolled compression, cutting storage/bandwidth for run-heavy data (framebuffers, telemetry, bitmap indexes).

edges.cite: Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications, ch. 4: backward/forward-compatible encodings (Protobuf/Thrift field tags) are what make rolling upgrades possible, with old and new code coexisting
edges.note: Mixed-version fleets require encodings both sides can read.
Tag-based skipping of unknown fields is the format-side counterpart of consumer-side tolerant reading.
Effective Java item 90: the proxy routes deserialization through real constructors so invariants are checked on untrusted byte streams - input validation for serialized data.

edges.cite: Fowler, PoEAA, Serialized LOB: persists a cluster of objects out of a Domain Model by serializing them into a single large object
edges.note: One persistence option for object-graph clusters of a domain model; honest scope - it is an option, not a dependency.

edges.cite: POSA1, Broker: marshaling and unmarshaling of requests and results is a stated Broker responsibility; the Serializer pattern (Riehle et al., PLoP) names RPC marshaling as a primary use
edges.note: Marshaling is the mechanism the Broker style's remote invocation depends on.

edges.cite: POSA4, Requestor: the requestor marshals invocations into transmittable messages (and Invoker unmarshals) - the Serializer mechanism
edges.note: The remoting middleware's marshaling duty is realized by a serializer component.
TDMA slot/frame alignment (TTP, FlexRay) depends on known sync patterns for clock and frame acquisition on the shared medium.
Physical/link-layer frame acquisition mechanism the layered stack sits on (preambles, start-of-frame patterns).

Consumers that extract only what they need and ignore unknown content let multiple service versions serve traffic simultaneously - Fowler's stated purpose (bliki: TolerantReader) mapped to the deployability tactic.

edges.cite: Bass/Clements/Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice (after Utas): the parameter-typing availability tactic is defined over type-length-value message parameters
edges.note: The tactic is literally stated in terms of TLV-encoded parameters.
The pervasive self-describing option/extension encoding of layered protocol headers (IP/TCP options, TLS extensions, BER).
The L in TLV is per-field length prefixing, which is what lets readers skip unknown records.
Small integers dominate real data; base-128 encoding cuts wire and storage size where it matters.

edges.cite: Protocol Buffers encoding documentation: the wire format is a varint-encoded field tag/wire-type followed by the payload
edges.note: Field tags themselves ride on varint encoding.

edges.cite: Protocol Buffers encoding documentation: sint32/sint64 apply ZigZag mapping so varint encoding stays short for negative values
edges.note: ZigZag exists to make varints efficient for signed data.
Keeps small-magnitude negative numbers short under varint encoding.
